newsitem.title: FRANCE: Spain, France favour possible Zaire force.
newsitem.headline: Spain, France favour possible Zaire force.

text.p: Spanish Foreign Minister Abel Matutes said on Monday that Paris and Madrid were in favour of considering the creation of an international force to guarantee distribution of humanitarian aid in Zaire.
He told reporters at a Franco-Spanish summit in the southern port city of Marseille that creating the force would need the support of the United Nations and the Organisation of African Unity.

It was apparently the first time that Western allies have spoken publicly about sending a military force to Zaire. Matutes said both Rwanda and Zaire would have to agree not to place obstacles in the way of distributing humanitarian aid.
"If these conditions exist, France and Spain are in favour of considering the creation of this force, for which the collaboration of the United States will also be very important," he said.
"Then we would have the minimum security conditions for this force to proceed with the distribution of humanitarian aid," he added.
French Foreign Minister Herve de Charette earlier said that France wanted talks to discuss ways of securing the area around refugee camps in eastern Zaire to allow humanitarian aid through.
